cases.title: Delhi: shared bidder credentials and missing award records
cases.question: Do documented bidder identifiers and missing award records survive legal-entity and transaction-level reconciliation?
cases.summary: August 2026 reporting of a CAG audit identifies shared bidder identifiers and sparse award disclosure. The investigation tests bid independence and publication completeness; affected tender values are not corruption-loss estimates. Related subsidy and GST findings are separate financial populations.

observations.text: The reported 2017–18 to 2022–23 audit found 14,527 valid bids in 7,181 tenders valued at ₹3,217.44 crore sharing IP addresses; 45 tenders worth ₹530.25 crore involved common PAN registrations. These populations may overlap.
Only 5,363 of approximately 155,000 tenders reportedly contained award details. Missing portal records do not prove no contract or missing expenditure.
Subsidy findings include ₹17.81 crore for more than 50,000 connections showing zero consumption for more than a year. This is a distinct subsidy-control question, not a bidder-network payment.

counterevidence.text: Shared gateways, authorised filing agents and duplicate registration histories can explain some common identifiers; the inspected reporting does not identify final collusion findings or beneficiaries.
The Assembly Speaker described PAC scrutiny and requested departmental action-taken notes; the inspected record does not establish their subsequent completion.

cases.title: Lucknow: verify completed meter refunds and the replacement roadmap
cases.question: Did the regulator’s completed refund population omit eligible accounts, and will the no-cost replacement roadmap be filed?
cases.summary: The August 27 regulatory disposal supersedes earlier stories of pending credits. The next test is reconciliation of 92,231 credited accounts, 907 exclusions and any omitted eligible connections, plus delivery of the required legacy-meter roadmap.

observations.text: The final reported reconciliation is 93,138 examined connections minus 907 non-overcharged STS accounts equals 92,231 credited eligible accounts, with ₹32.74 crore in the original paragraph 17 table and ₹32.75 crore in paragraph 22. The later news report matches the table. Both original values are retained; no exact reconciled total is asserted.
Earlier 11 August proceedings described 6,188 still-uncredited accounts and missed filing deadlines; this earlier status must not be presented as current after the disposal order.

Paragraph 21 directs a roadmap within two months for replacing all keypad/token meters, including 907 existing STS meters. Paragraph 20 quotes the 21 November 2025 tariff-order no-additional-cost requirement; paragraph 21 records UPPCL’s statement that 907 meters predated an order described there as 22 November 2025. The document’s one-day date discrepancy is preserved.

counterevidence.text: UPPCL attributed interim pricing to the absence of a revised cost-data book and invoked central smart-meter policy; the regulator rejected that as authority for the excess recovery.
The case was disposed after reported credits and exclusion of 907 accounts that were not overcharged. No unresolved ₹33 crore balance should be fabricated.

Order paragraphs 14–16 record UPPCL’s explanation that 373,509 connections was the gross Jhatpat population including non-smart meters, while 93,138 was the examined refund cohort. The larger total is not proof of omitted refunds.

cases.title: Jaipur: certificate warnings, tender approvals and alleged intermediaries
cases.question: Were qualification warnings received before approvals and alleged onward transfers, and can each claimed step survive the defence and original records?
cases.summary: The 29 September 2026 Supreme Court bail order documents a prosecution theory involving qualification certificates, two contracting firms and an alleged intermediary route. It grants Badaya and Dixit bail and expressly leaves every factual allegation to trial. Joshi’s 2025 PMLA bail and 2026 ACB bail proceedings are tracked separately.

observations.text: SC paragraph 5 recites the allegation that Shri Ganpati Tubewell Company and Shri Shyam Tubewell Company used forged IRCON certificates to obtain approximately 104 tenders worth ₹979.45 crore. This is alleged contract scope, not quantified proven loss.

SC paragraph 7(a) records an allegation that Shubhanshu Dixit failed to act on 2023 complaints while participating in finance-committee processes. His recorded office period is 30 December 2022 to 13 February 2024.

SC paragraph 7(b) recites an alleged Badaya-mediated route through unnamed relatives/acquaintances to Sumangalam Landmark LLP; no account numbers, identities of unnamed people or transaction amounts are inferred.

The 2025 PMLA order records the agency’s separate corporate-route account naming Mugdog Packaging India LLP, Maxclenz Retail PvtLtd and Jay The Victory before Sumangalam LLP. It does not establish pairwise transaction order, corporate identifiers or equivalence with the 2026 LLP label.

counterevidence.text: SC granted Badaya and Dixit bail on 29 September 2026: investigation against them complete, evidence seized, charges not yet framed and lengthy trial expected. Paragraph 18 disclaims any opinion on merits or evidentiary value.

Joshi’s counsel said he caused suspensions, blacklisting and FIRs, disputed personal benefit, and said he was not a member of bid-evaluation or finance committees. These responses require checking against dated decision records.

Joshi obtained PMLA bail 3 December 2025; reported ACB bail refusal 13 August 2026 is a distinct proceeding. Badaya/Dixit’sSeptember relief does not change Joshi’s ACB status; no later outcome was established by the cutoff search.

cases.title: Chandigarh: recurring Punjab procurement controls after PAC assurances
cases.question: Were prior PAC assurances converted into enforceable system controls and tender-level remedial decisions?
cases.summary: The Punjab e-procurement audit compares 2018–2023 records with weaknesses reported in 2017. Chandigarh is the state administrative research hub, not the site of every audited tender. The new watch tests documented remediation rather than treating common credentials as proof of collusion.

observations.text: The audit analysed 1,85,920 tenders and examined 494 selected tenders across 111 procuring entities; the documentary sample and database population are different denominators.

In the PWD first-instance single-bid cohort, 1130 tenders received one bid and 383 received awards; a separate 424 single-qualified-bid cohort produced 397 awards. These categories must not be assumed disjoint or summed as losses.
Table 2.12 reports up to 214 registered bidders sharing an email, 83 a mobile number and 135 a PAN. These are maximum registrations per credential, not counts of proven collusive bidders.
The chapter records the previous PAC assurance, missing automated single-bid restrictions, and aNovember 2024 advisory. That is a testable policy-to-system implementation gap.

counterevidence.text: The nodal department stated individual user departments made award decisions and said it issued an advisory. CAG considered an advisory insufficient because business rules needed system integration.

Shared service providers or duplicate registrations may explain some credential overlap; exact legal identity and tender-specific conduct require separate evidence. Audit-era weaknesses are not verified current vulnerabilities.

cases.title: Dehradun: paid smart assets, operating costs and recovery follow-through
cases.question: Were non-functional assets made operational and identified recoveries completed after management accepted the audit recommendations?
cases.summary: The Smart Cities audit describes a measurable gap between capital spending and usable services, including school equipment without affordable electricity. It also documents successful water SCADA and other benefits. March 2026 tabling is recent disclosure of older expenditure; no fresh July–October remediation record was found.

observations.text: Against ₹737.50 crore released, ₹634.11 crore expenditure was reported for 2016–17 to 2022–23. These are programme totals, not irregularity totals.
A ₹4.55 crore waste-monitoring module remained unused toFebruary 2025; ₹5.91 crore school smart equipment was non-functional because schools could not afford operating electricity.
The summary records ₹5.19 crore consultant-payment irregularities and ₹19.06 crore unutilised agency funds not recovered, with distinct financial scopes.

counterevidence.text: CAG observed improved traffic and safety management and successful SCADA water-supply implementation; the entire programme was not a failure.
Management agreed to all 12 recommendations. Work-site encumbrances and cross-department coordination contributed to delays, providing alternatives to corrupt-intent assumptions.

cases.title: Patna: prospective watch on ₹62.52 crore police-vehicle approval
cases.question: Will the approved crowd-control vehicles have documented need, competitive awards, delivery verification and lifecycle-cost justification?
cases.summary: The 30 September 2026 cabinet decision provides a prospective baseline before known awards: 30 water cannons and 86 Vajra vehicles. It is a procurement-monitoring case, with no evidence here of corrupt awards or named supplier benefits.

observations.text: Administrative approval totals ₹62.52 crore: 30× ₹88 lakh= ₹26.40 crore and 86× ₹42 lakh= ₹36.12 crore. The amounts are approval estimates, not verified payments.
The Home Department cited festivals, rallies, VIP movements, riots and emergencies. The approval follows formation of district anti-riot units.
Reported state riot counts declined from 9,419 in 2020 to 2,502 in 2025. That challenges a simplistic rising-riots justification but does not establish fleet requirements or misuse.

counterevidence.text: Fleet age, regional coverage, replacement needs and emergency duties can justify capacity despite falling incident counts. Neither inspected report provides inventory data or evidence of a tainted award.
No vendor, tender outcome, disbursement or minister-to-company financial link is established; the graph stops at the administrative decision.
